title.narrative: Nationwide Initiative to Combat GBV Against Women in Sri Lanka – Empowering Women and Advancing Gender Equality Through Grassroots Leadership

description.narrative:
Gender-based violence (GBV), particularly intimate partner violence (IPV), remains a pervasive and significantly underreported problem across Sri Lanka. Despite legal frameworks such as the Prevention of Domestic Violence Act (2005), survivors routinely face systemic barriers: limited awareness of rights, deep-rooted social stigma, fragmented support infrastructure, financial dependency on abusers, inconsistent policy enforcement, and compounded discrimination for marginalized groups. This project provides holistic, sustainable solutions through education, advocacy, capacity building, and survivor services, empowering women aged 15 to 45 to break cycles of abuse and reclaim autonomy over their lives.
Primary Aim of the project is to reduce intimate partner violence across Sri Lanka by educating, empowering, and supporting women survivors, whilst advocating for stronger legal and policy interventions, promoting gender equality, and addressing the structural factors that exclude women and girls. The secondary aim is to strengthen women’s rights, promote gender equality, and empower structurally excluded groups of women and girls through direct interventions, advocacy, and capacity-building at the grassroots level.
Project Objectives - Educate women and communities on GBV, IPV, legal rights, and available support networks. - Provide survivor-centred services (counselling, shelter, and legal aid). - Strengthen survivors' capacity for independence and leadership. - Conduct advocacy campaigns to shift societal attitudes and push for policy reforms. - Engage key stakeholders (local authorities, healthcare providers, and community leaders). - Combat structural discrimination perpetuating gender inequality through community dialogue.
